questions.scenario: A projectile is launched from the origin with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal.
questions.question: Calculate the Cartesian equation of the trajectory.
marking_criteria: Correct application of initial velocity components
Correct substitution into the trajectory equation
Correct algebraic manipulation to express y in terms of x
hints: Break down the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components using trigonometry.
questions.model_answer:
Initial velocity components: vx = 20 * cos(30) = 10√3 m/s, vy = 20 * sin(30) = 10 m/s.
Equation of motion: y = x * tan(30) - (g/(2*(vx^2))) * x^2.
Substitute g = 9.8 m/s^2 and simplify to get: y = (√3/3)x - (4.9/(2*(10√3)^2)) * x^2.
questions.explanation: You correctly calculated the horizontal and vertical components of the initial velocity and then used these to derive the Cartesian equation of the trajectory.
questions.topic_label: The Cartesian equation of the trajectory

questions.scenario: A projectile is launched from the origin with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal.
questions.question: Find the maximum height reached by the projectile.
marking_criteria: Correct identification of the maximum height point
Correct application of the trajectory equation to find height
hints: Stay focused on this: Find the maximum height reached by the projectile — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Correct application of the trajectory to find height.
questions.model_answer:
At maximum height, vy = 0. Use vy = vy_initial - g*t. t = vy_initial / g = 10 / 9.8 ≈ 1.02 s.
Substitute t into the y component of the position equation: y = 10 * 1.02 - 4.9*(1.02)^2 ≈ 5.1 m.
questions.explanation: You correctly determined the time at which the maximum height is reached and then used this time to find the height.
questions.topic_label: The Cartesian equation of the trajectory (Projectiles)

questions.scenario: A projectile is launched from a cliff 30 metres above the ground with an initial velocity of 15 m/s at an angle of 45 degrees to the horizontal.
questions.question: Find the range of the projectile.
marking_criteria: Correct identification of the range condition
Correct application of the trajectory equation to find the range
Correct algebraic manipulation to solve for x
hints: The range is the horizontal distance travelled when the projectile returns to the ground level.
questions.model_answer:
Set y = 0 in the equation y = x + 30 - (4.9/(2*(15/√2)^2)) * x^2.
0 = x + 30 - (4.9/(2*(15/√2)^2)) * x^2.
Solve the quadratic equation to find x: x ≈ 21.21 m.
questions.explanation: You correctly set up the equation to find the range and solved the quadratic equation to find the horizontal distance.
